cells.verb: taking the next step by the little light you have, without forcing the rest of the road to show itself
cells.place: in the clearing you make when you set something down on purpose
cells.ask: Let one of those next steps point somewhere. Not a plan — just the direction you'd move if you moved from what you actually feel about it. The dreaming already comes from what you've lived; it can afford a destination.
cells.core: You're putting things down and walking on without needing to see where the path goes. The letting go isn't flinching and the not-knowing isn't drifting — you've lived enough of this to trust what the next step shows you, and only the next step. What you imagine from here isn't escape. It's made of what you've already been through.
cells.sheetLine: You let go and step forward by what little you can see, and it holds.

cells.tense: Future — bracing at a road that hasn't been written yet.
cells.verb: reading every patch of fog as a message, so the picture of the road replaces the walking
cells.place: in a letting go that has turned into a dream about having let go
cells.ask: Tend one real thing today — something actually growing, that you can touch and water — without deciding what it means. Hold it loosely, the way you'd hold something alive. The dreaming comes back honest once it's rooted in what you've lived, not in what you've foretold.
cells.core: You've stopped setting things down and started imagining the empty room. Somewhere ahead is the version where it all fell away and the meaning became clear, and you're living there — so each uncertainty becomes a sign, each loss becomes a chapter, and nothing has to actually leave your hands. The picture has gotten so rich it's doing the releasing for you.
cells.sheetLine: You're dreaming the clearing instead of making it.

cells.tense: Past — still standing at a door that's already behind you.
cells.verb: refusing to take a step you can't see all the way to the end of
cells.place: in a letting go you won't allow until the whole road is lit
cells.ask: Pick out one thing you already know matters, before you can say why, and let that count — no argument, no proof. Set down one thing on the strength of it. The dreaming returns when the knowing is allowed in; it's made of what you've already lived through.
cells.core: You won't put anything down until you can see exactly what you'll pick up instead. Something back there taught you that the half-seen path couldn't be trusted, and you're still standing at that door — asking for the whole map before you'll take one step, calling the quiet pull toward the next thing a trick. The grip isn't strength. It's the step you haven't taken yet.
cells.sheetLine: You won't let go until you can see the whole road, and so you don't.

cells.tense: Disowned present — pen down in a room you're already writing.
cells.verb: steering by a picture of where you're going that you'd deny having
cells.place: in a letting go you call things just falling away
cells.ask: Keep one small practice alone: each morning, write the one thing you'd choose if you were choosing. No pressure on it — just the same quiet minute, kept. The hand steering shows up in the repetition, and the dreaming becomes yours, made from what you've actually lived.
cells.core: Things keep leaving your hands, and you talk about it as if they left on their own. But something is choosing what stays and what goes, and it's choosing by an image of the road you haven't let yourself look at. You're already imagining your way through this. The letting go is yours; you just haven't signed it.
cells.sheetLine: You're already dreaming your way out of this. You call it drifting.
